convert the f/3.65 fiber output to f/8 using two cemented doublet lenses and a singlet lens
tics tube, which increases the f-ratio from f/3.65 to f/8.1

rows.note: The magnification is not stated as a number in S20. DERIVED: an imaging relay with a real focus and telecentric input and output changes the f-ratio by its magnification, so m = 7.95 / 3.6 = 2.21 (K23's 8.1 / 3.65 = 2.22 agrees to 0.5 percent): the HR fiber image at the collimator focus is 64.1 um x 2.21 = 141.5 um and HE 101.2 um -> 223.5 um. Cross-check with S16 Sec. 2.3 in the next row. S20 gives the C4 variant a '<3% variation' of the fiber magnification (Fig. 9 caption) but its Table 1 gives C4 6.3-6.4 percent; the chosen C3 is 4.4 percent. The magnification therefore varies by about 4 percent across 380-930 nm (SOURCED, Table 1); the explorer uses the mean.

imaged on to the fold mirror (M2) by the parabola (M1) after being dispersed by the R4 echelle grating

rows.note: SETTLED by S20 (was INFERRED from S16 and the figure). The 5 deg is the OAP off-axis angle, the deflection between the injected chief ray and the collimated beam (the beam leaves parallel to the parent axis). In the explorer's convention a mirror tilted by tau turns the beam by 2 tau (the DEIMOS rule: tilt = half the angle between incoming chief ray and returned beam), so colTilt = 2.5 deg (DERIVED). The direction is the CROSS-dispersion direction, i.e. perpendicular to the plane of S16 Fig. 2 (a plan view in the dispersion plane), which supersedes the earlier in-plane reading of about 4 deg MEASURED from that figure (an in-plane estimate that the text does not support). The echelle's gamma = 0.5 deg is a separate, much smaller tilt. Not a Schmidt collimator: colTilt is not 0.

Per-order span = full 9216-px trace, DERIVED: order 170 span 69.12 A / 9216 px = 0.0075 A/px (0.75 A/mm), center 3605.5 A, R_sample = 3605.5 / 0.0075 / 5 = 96,000 per 5 px (the design 'one resolution element = 5 pixels').
